order.Dietary: No meat: swap guanciale for tofu. Eats eggs and dairy.
order.Requests: Roman-style, so no cream. Extra-crispy tofu.
order.Target time: 25 minutes (sim time) from order to service
order.Printed ticket text:
#014  T6  2 COVERS
2x SPAGH CARBONARA (ROMAN)
  ** NO MEAT -> TOFU **
  tofu extra crispy
19:42
order.Setting: Evening service. The ticket printer chatters; the ticket slides onto the rail above the counter.
order.Customer line 1: "Hi! Could we get two of the carbonara in Roman-style, please?"
order.Customer line 2: "Neither of us eats meat, though. Could you do it with tofu instead of the guanciale?"
order.Customer line 3: "If the tofu could be extra crispy, that would be amazing."
order.Server line (to kitchen): "Two carbonara for Table 6. Roman-style. No meat, tofu instead. Extra-crispy tofu!"
order.Nonna Pina intro (modal): "A tofu carbonara! Same technique, new star. Read the ticket carefully: every word on it changes something we do. Ready?"
order.Goal 1: Adapt a recipe to a dietary requirement without losing what makes it work.
order.Goal 2: Understand why tofu is pressed and fried in hot oil while guanciale starts in a cold pan.
order.Goal 3: Build an emulsion from egg, cheese, fat and starchy pasta water, with no cream.
order.Goal 4: Control egg temperature: thickens at ~62 °C, scrambles above 70 °C.
order.Success criteria: Silky, glossy sauce; crisp tofu; well seasoned, not salty; served within the target time.

substeps.title: Open the tofu pack
substeps.left: Open the tofu pack to drain the packing water.
substeps.right: 2 Kitchen Towels, Cast-iron Skillet (not usable yet)
substeps.learning: Packing water has to go before pressing can draw out the water inside.
substeps.sceneState: Tofu package on the board.

texts.T-TOWELS: Open the pack and drain it before anything else.
texts.E-WEIGHT: Open the pack and drain it before anything else.

substeps.title: Press the tofu
substeps.left: Draw out moisture from the tofu.
substeps.learning: Water on the surface turns to steam and stops browning. Dry tofu crisps; wet tofu steams.
substeps.sceneState: Drained tofu block on the board.

wrongSpot.T-TOWELS: One towel under the tofu, one on top. Try again.
wrongSpot.E-WEIGHT: The Cast-iron Skillet goes on top of the tofu to press it.

substeps.title: Choose the pressing time
substeps.left: Select the appropriate pressing time for draining the tofu.
substeps.learning: 15-20 minutes removes most surface water. Use the time to get the pasta water on.
substeps.sceneState: Tofu stack with weight on top.
substeps.notes: Timer fast-forwards; the scene shows water pooling on the towel.

substeps.title: Cut the tofu into cubes
substeps.left: Select the appropriate cuts for evenly sized pieces that crisp well.
substeps.right: The cuts as a pick-all-that-apply list
substeps.passRule: Tick A-2.4-01 to 03 (multi-select), then Check; they animate in order.
substeps.incomplete: Something’s missing. Which cuts get you all the way to 1 cm cubes?
substeps.learning: Even 1 cm cubes cook at the same rate and give the most crisp surface per bite.
substeps.sceneState: Pressed tofu block on the board.
substeps.notes: Cutting pattern: slabs, then strips, then cubes.
substeps.mixedMissing: =Too big. 3 cm chunks crisp outside but stay soft inside. And you'll need more cuts to get to even 1 cm cubes.

substeps.title: Season the tofu
substeps.left: Select the appropriate seasoning for a savoury, smoky flavour.
substeps.learning: Soy sauce adds savoury depth (umami); smoked paprika adds smokiness. Go light: pecorino is already very salty.
substeps.sceneState: Tofu cubes in a bowl.
substeps.notes: Optional substep: skipping it gives a Degraded 'bland' note.

substeps.title: Fill the pasta pot
substeps.left: Fill the pot with enough water for the pasta to move freely.
substeps.learning: Lots of water stays at the boil when the pasta goes in, and gives the strands room so they don't stick.
substeps.sceneState: Pot on the counter next to the sink.

texts.E-KNOB-BACK: Fill the pot with water first.
texts.T-LID: Fill the pot with water first.

wrongSpot.T-POT: The pot needs to go under the tap. Put it in the sink.

substeps.title: Bring the water to the boil
substeps.left: Bring the water to a fast boil.
substeps.learning: Water takes about 10 minutes to boil, so start it early and prep while it heats.
substeps.sceneState: Filled pot in the sink.
substeps.notes: Salt goes in later (S6.1), once the water boils.

substeps.title: Choose how to start the pan
substeps.left: Select the appropriate way to start the pan for crisp tofu.
substeps.right: Four ways to start the pan
substeps.learning: Guanciale starts cold so its fat can melt out slowly. Tofu has almost no fat, so it needs hot oil to crisp instead of stick.
substeps.sceneState: Empty skillet on the front burner; burner off.
substeps.notes: Key adaptation moment from guanciale to tofu.

substeps.title: Heat the oil
substeps.left: Heat the oil to frying temperature.
substeps.right: Olive oil, smoked paprika, tongs (only the oil is usable yet)
substeps.passRule: Actions A-4.2 in order; heat inside the target range.
substeps.learning: Browning (the Maillard reaction) starts around 140 °C. Shimmering oil is hot enough to seal the tofu straight away.
substeps.sceneState: Skillet on the front burner; heat knob at Off.

texts.I-TOFU: Wait for the shimmer, or the tofu will stick.

wrongSpot.I-OIL: The oil goes into the skillet.

substeps.title: Fry the tofu until golden
substeps.left: Fry the tofu until crisp and golden on all sides.
substeps.right: Tongs, soy sauce, smoked paprika (timer options open in the scene)
substeps.passRule: Actions A-4.3 in order; wait times inside the target ranges.
substeps.learning: Moving the tofu too soon tears the crust before it forms. Paprika burns fast, so it goes in at the very end.
substeps.sceneState: Shimmering oil in the skillet; tofu cubes on the board.

wrongSpot.I-TOFU: The tofu goes into the hot skillet.

substeps.title: Lift out the tofu, keep the oil
substeps.left: Take the tofu out.
substeps.learning: The oil now carries flavour and becomes the fat in the sauce emulsion. Tofu goes back in at the end so it stays crisp.
substeps.sceneState: Crisp tofu in the skillet; burner on.

wrongSpot.T-SKILLET: Put the tofu on the resting plate so it stays crisp.

substeps.stepTitle: Prepare the Egg and Cheese Mixture
substeps.title: Choose the eggs
substeps.left: Select the appropriate eggs for a rich sauce for two.
substeps.learning: Yolks bring richness and colour; a couple of whole eggs make the sauce looser and easier to handle. Rule: 1 whole + 1 yolk per person, plus 1 yolk 'for the pot'.
substeps.sceneState: Egg carton and empty bowl on the counter.

substeps.stepTitle: Prepare the Egg and Cheese Mixture
substeps.title: Crack and separate the eggs
substeps.left: Add the eggs to the bowl for the sauce base.
substeps.learning: Egg whites set at a lower temperature than yolks, which is one reason extra yolks make a more forgiving sauce.
substeps.sceneState: Bowl and egg carton on the counter.

substeps.stepTitle: Prepare the Egg and Cheese Mixture
substeps.title: Pick the grater
substeps.left: Select the appropriate grater side for cheese that melts smoothly.
substeps.learning: Powder-fine cheese melts evenly into the egg. Coarse shreds clump and turn stringy.
substeps.sceneState: Box grater and a wedge of pecorino on the counter.

substeps.stepTitle: Prepare the Egg and Cheese Mixture
substeps.title: Grate, season and whisk
substeps.left: Combine the cheese and pepper with the eggs into a smooth paste.
substeps.learning: Freshly cracked pepper is a main flavour here, not a garnish.
substeps.sceneState: Bowl with eggs.
substeps.notes: No salt: the cheese brings plenty.

shortHold.I-PECORINO: Keep going. You need about 150 g for the sauce to coat the pasta.

substeps.title: Salt the water
substeps.left: Select the appropriate amount of salt for seasoning the pasta water.
substeps.learning: Pasta absorbs salt as it cooks. Salt more lightly than usual for carbonara: the pecorino and soy are salty, and the water goes into the sauce.
substeps.sceneState: Pot at a rolling boil.

substeps.title: Add the spaghetti
substeps.left: Cook the pasta in the salted water without it sticking.
substeps.right: Coarse salt, spaghetti, olive oil, tongs
substeps.learning: Stirring in the first minute stops the strands sticking while their surface starch is gelatinising.
substeps.sceneState: Water at a rolling boil.

wrongSpot.I-SALT: That goes into the boiling pot.
wrongSpot.I-SPAGHETTI: That goes into the boiling pot.

substeps.title: Decide when to pull the pasta
substeps.left: Select the appropriate time to take the pasta out for finishing it in the pan.
substeps.learning: The pasta keeps cooking in the pan with the sauce, so it comes out a minute before al dente.
substeps.sceneState: Spaghetti boiling; timer running.
substeps.notes: Timer fast-forwards to the chosen minute.

substeps.title: Move the pasta into the pan
substeps.left: Move the pasta into the pan, keeping some cooking water aside.
substeps.learning: Starchy pasta water is the glue that binds fat and egg. It's your insurance if the sauce gets too thick.
substeps.sceneState: Pasta near al dente; skillet with flavoured oil.

wrongSpot.T-TONGS: The pasta goes into the skillet with the flavoured oil.

substeps.title: Temper the eggs
substeps.left: Temper the egg mixture so it pours like cream.
substeps.learning: Tempering warms the eggs gradually so they aren't shocked by the hot pan. You can always thicken a sauce, but you can't unscramble one.
substeps.sceneState: Egg paste in the bowl; pasta in the skillet.

substeps.title: Deal with the heat
substeps.left: Select the appropriate heat level for adding the eggs.
substeps.learning: Egg yolk starts to thicken around 62 °C and scrambles above 70 °C. A pan on the flame is far hotter than that.
substeps.sceneState: Pasta tossing in the pan on low heat.

substeps.title: Toss into a silky sauce
substeps.left: Toss the pasta with the eggs into a silky sauce, then plate it.
substeps.right: Toss speed, heat on/off, splash of pasta water, Plate it; live sauce thermometer
substeps.passRule: Actions A-7.4-01 to 03 in order; sauce must end Silky (thickened, no curds).
substeps.learning: Thicken with gentle heat, loosen with pasta water. Constant movement keeps any one spot from overheating.
substeps.sceneState: Pan off the heat; pasta coated in oil.
substeps.notes: Live sim: speed control, heat on/off, splash water, Plate button.

substeps.title: Choose the toppings
substeps.left: Select the appropriate toppings for a classic finish.
substeps.passRule: All Correct items selected and no Incorrect items.
substeps.incomplete: Missing something. A Roman carbonara is finished with two things from the ingredients you already have.
substeps.learning: Keep it simple: the toppings repeat the dish's own flavours.
substeps.sceneState: Two warm bowls on the counter.
substeps.multiWrong: {items} would cover up the flavours this dish is built on. A Roman carbonara is finished simply, with things already on your counter.
substeps.mixedMissing: And the classic finish is still missing something.

substeps.title: Plate the pasta
substeps.left: Plate the pasta with its toppings.
substeps.right: Tongs, black peppercorns, pecorino, kitchen timer
substeps.learning: Carbonara keeps thickening as it cools. Plate it fast.
substeps.sceneState: Finished pasta in the pan; crisp tofu on the resting plate.

texts.E-BELL: Plate and top both bowls first.

wrongSpot.T-TONGS: The pasta goes into the serving bowls.

substeps.title: Serve
substeps.left: Serve the dish while it's hot.
substeps.learning: Carbonara keeps thickening as it cools. Serve it immediately.

options.label: 5 minutes

options.feedback: Perfect.

options.label: 45 minutes
options.feedback: It would be very dry, but Table 6 would be gone by then! 15-20 minutes does the job.

options.label: Toss with 1 tsp soy sauce and a pinch of smoked paprika
options.feedback: Savoury and a little smoky. That's our guanciale stand-in. We'll add the paprika at the end of frying so it doesn't burn.

options.label: Salt it generously
options.feedback: Careful. Pecorino is very salty, so the dish will be over-salted.

options.label: Soak it in 4 tbsp soy sauce
options.feedback: Too much liquid. We just pressed the water out! Now it won't crisp, and it'll be very salty.

options.label: Leave it plain
options.feedback: It will work, but plain tofu is mild. A little seasoning gives the dish its savoury backbone.

options.label: Cold pan, no oil, then heat up
options.feedback: That's the rule for guanciale, because it brings its own fat. Tofu has none, so it would weld itself to the pan.

options.label: Cold pan with oil, then heat up, wait until it shimmers
options.feedback: The tofu would soak up oil as it slowly warms and turn greasy instead of crisp.

options.label: Heat the pan on medium, add 2 tbsp oil, wait until it shimmers
options.feedback: Yes! Hot oil seals the surface straight away, so it browns instead of sticking.

options.label: Heat the empty pan on high until it smokes, then add 2 tbsp oil
options.feedback: Too hot. Oil would burn the moment it went in, and the tofu would char outside and stay cold inside.

options.label: 2 whole eggs + 3 yolks

options.label: 4 whole eggs
options.feedback: It works, but more whites mean a paler, looser sauce that sets sooner.

options.label: 2 yolks only

options.label: 6 whole eggs and a splash of cream

options.label: None

options.label: Half a cup
options.feedback: That's seawater! The pasta and the pasta water, which goes into the sauce, are now inedibly salty.

options.label: Turn it up so the sauce thickens faster

options.label: Freshly Cracked Black Pepper

options.label: A Dusting of Pecorino
options.feedback: Yes. A little more on top.

options.label: Chopped Parsley
options.feedback: Not on a Roman carbonara. Let's keep it classic.

options.label: A Drizzle of Cream

options.label: Chilli Flakes

T-1.1.title: Assessing Customer's Request
T-1.1.text: Notice how the order shapes the dish: dietary needs change the ingredients, and a request like 'Roman-style' changes the method.

T-1.3.title: Deciding the Ingredients
T-1.3.text: Real carbonara is pasta, eggs, pecorino, black pepper and a cured meat. Today tofu takes the meat's place. Creaminess comes from technique and not the cream.

T-2.1.title: Preparing the Tofu
T-2.1.text: Tofu is mostly water. Press it under a weight to remove the moisture from it before cooking.

T-2.4.title: Cutting the Tofu
T-2.4.text: Cut 1 cm cubes. Even pieces brown at the same rate ensuring that the customer has a consistent experience when eating the tofu.

T-2.5.title: Borrowing guanciale's flavour
T-2.5.text: Guanciale is salty, smoky and savoury. A splash of soy and a pinch of smoked paprika get the tofu part of the way there. Go easy on salt: pecorino is very salty.

T-3.1.title: Boiling the Water
T-3.1.text: A big pot of water takes about 10 minutes to boil. Get it going now, and the rest of the prep fits around it.

T-4.1.title: Not every rule transfers
T-4.1.text: Guanciale goes into a cold pan so its fat melts out slowly. Tofu has no fat to give. Think about what tofu needs instead.

T-4.4.title: Reusing the Oil
T-4.4.text: The oil in the pan now tastes of crispy, smoky tofu. It becomes the fat in your sauce, so don't pour it away.

T-5.2.title: Yolks for richness
T-5.2.text: Extra yolks make the sauce golden, rich and more forgiving, because yolks set at a higher temperature than whites.

T-5.3.title: Finer is better
T-5.3.text: The finer the cheese, the faster and more evenly it melts into the egg. Coarse shreds go stringy and clump.

T-6.1.title: Seasoning the Water
T-6.1.text: Pasta water should taste seasoned, not like the sea. In carbonara, go lighter: the water ends up in a sauce full of salty pecorino.

T-6.3.title: One minute early
T-6.3.text: Pull the pasta a minute before al dente. It finishes cooking in the pan while the sauce comes together.

T-7.1.title: Never drain carbonara pasta
T-7.1.text: Save a mug of pasta water first, then lift the pasta straight into the pan with tongs. The starchy water binds the sauce.

T-7.2.title: Temper the eggs
T-7.2.text: Whisk a little hot pasta water into the eggs before they go near the pan. It warms them gently, so they thicken instead of scrambling.

T-7.3.title: The magic numbers
T-7.3.text: Egg yolk thickens at about 62 °C and scrambles above 70 °C. A pan on the flame is over 150 °C. The pasta's own heat is usually enough.

T-7.4.title: Keep it moving
T-7.4.text: Toss constantly. Too thin? Brief, gentle heat. Too thick or too hot? A splash of pasta water. You can always thicken a sauce, but you can't unscramble one.

T-8.2.title: Serve it now
T-8.2.text: Carbonara thickens as it cools. Plate it, top it, and get it to the table straight away.

outcomes.title: Nonna-approved
outcomes.reaction: Saumya: "This is incredible. Crispy tofu, silky sauce, and not a drop of cream. Can I get the recipe?"
outcomes.nonna: Perfetto. That's a real carbonara, tofu and all.
outcomes.notes: Recap all steps; unlock 'Carbonara master' badge.

outcomes.title: Very good
outcomes.reaction: Saumya: "Really tasty! Maybe just a touch [saltier / thicker / softer] than I'd expect."
outcomes.nonna: Good work. One or two things to tighten up.
outcomes.notes: Show the Degraded notes as 'Next time'.

outcomes.title: Edible
outcomes.reaction: Saumya: "Thanks, it's... fine. The sauce was a bit off."
outcomes.nonna: It's dinner. Let's look at what went sideways.
outcomes.notes: Show the Degraded notes and offer to replay those steps.

outcomes.title: Sent back
outcomes.reaction: Saumya: "Sorry, I don't think I can finish this."
outcomes.nonna: Every cook has nights like this. Let's try again.

outcomes.trigger: S6.1 half a cup of salt
outcomes.title: Too salty to serve
outcomes.nonna: Seawater pasta can't be saved. Salt lightly: the cheese does the rest.

outcomes.title: Burnt tofu
outcomes.reaction: (Smoke alarm; dish never leaves the kitchen.)
outcomes.nonna: Burnt oil turns everything bitter. Medium heat, and patience.

outcomes.trigger: S7.3 heat turned up, or S7.4 sauce held above 70 °C
outcomes.title: Scrambled eggs
outcomes.nonna: Above 70 °C the yolk sets into curds. Off the heat, keep tossing, and use that pasta water.
